title: Which servants of God we worship
source_text: Εἶτ᾿ οἴεται ἐκ τοῦ θρησκεύειν ἡμᾶς μετὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἀκολουθεῖν ἡμῖν τὸ καὶ καθ᾿ ἡμᾶς οὐ μόνον τὸν θεὸν ἀλλὰ καὶ τοὺς ὑπηρέτας αὐτοῦ θεραπεύεσθαι. εἰ μὲν οὖν ἐνόει τοὺς ἀληθῶς ὑπηρέτας τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ τὸν μονογενῆ τοῦ θεοῦ. τὸν Γαβριὴλ καὶ τὸν Μιχαὴλ καὶ τοὺς λοιποὺς ἀγγέλους [ἀρχαγγέλους]. καὶ τούτους ἔλεγε δεῖν θεραπεύεσθαι. ἴσως ἂν τὸ περὶ τοῦ θεραπεύειν αὐτοῦ σημαινόμενον ἐκκαθήραντες καὶ τῶν τοῦ θεραπεύοντος πράξεων εἴπομεν ἂν εἰς τὸν τόπον ὡς περὶ τηλικούτων διαλεγόμενοι ἅπερ ἐχωροῦμεν περὶ αὐτῶν νοῆσαι· νυνὶ δὲ ὑπηρέτας νομίζων τοὺς προσκυνουμένους ὑπὸ τῶν ἐθνῶν δαίμονας οὐχ ὑπάγει ἡμᾶς ἀκολουθίᾳ τῇ περὶ τοῦ θεραπεύειν τοὺς τοιούτους. οὓς ὑπηρέτας τοῦ πονηροῦ ὁ λόγος ἀποδείκνυσι καὶ ἄρχοντος τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου, ἀφιστάντος ἀπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ οὓς ἂν δύνηται. ὡς οὐχ ὑπηρέτας οὖν, οὓς οἱ λοιποὶ ἄνθρωποι σέβουσι, πάντας σέβειν καὶ θεραπεύειν ἐκκλίνομεν· οὐκ ἂν γὰρ ὑπηρέτας αὐτοὺς διδαχθέντες εἶναι τοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεοῦ ἐλέγομεν εἶναι δαιμόνια. διὸ τὸν ἕνα θεὸν καὶ τὸν ἕνα υἱὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ λόγον καὶ εἰκόνα ταῖς κατὰ τὸ δυνατὸν ἡμῖν ἱκεσίαις καὶ ἀξιώσεσι σέβομεν, προσάγοντες τῷ θεῷ τῶν ὅλων τὰς εὐχὰς διὰ τοῦ μονογενοῦς αὐτοῦ· ᾧ πρῶτον προσφέρομεν αὐτὰς, ἀξιοῦντες αὐτὸν „ἱλασμὸν“ ὄντα „τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν“ προσαγαγεῖν ὡς ἀρχιερέα τὰς εὐχὰς καὶ τὰς θυσίας καὶ τὰς ἐντεύξεις ἡμῶν τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεῷ. περὶ τὸν θεὸν οὖν ἡ πίστις ἡμῶν διὰ τοῦ ταύτην βεβαιοῦντος ἐν ἡμῖν υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, καὶ οὐδεμίαν ἡμῶν ἔχει δεῖξαι στάσιν περὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ ὁ Κέλσος. καὶ σέβομέν γε τὸν πατέρα, θαυμάζοντες αὐτοῦ τὸν υἱὸν λόγον καὶ σοφίαν καὶ ἀλήθειαν καὶ δικαιοσύνην καὶ πάντα, ἅπερ εἶναι μεμαθήκαμεν τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ, οὕτω δὴ καὶ τὸν γεννηθέντα ἀπὸ τοιούτου του πατρός. καὶ ταῦτα μὲν ταύτῃ.
pass_a_gloss: Then he thinks that from our worshipping (θρησκεύειν) with God His Son, it follows (ἀκολουθεῖν) for us that also according to us not only God but also His servants (ὑπηρέτας) are worshipped (θεραπεύεσθαι). If then he meant those truly servants of God after the Only-begotten (μονογενῆ) of God, Gabriel and Michael and the rest of the angels [archangels, bracketed], and said these too must be worshipped, perhaps, having cleansed/cleared (ἐκκαθήραντες) the meaning (σημαινόμενον) about his 'to worship' and the acts (πράξεων) of the one worshipping, we would have said on the topic (εἰς τὸν τόπον), as discussing about such great things, what we had capacity (ἐχωροῦμεν) to understand about them. But now, considering as servants the demons (δαίμονας) bowed down to (προσκυνουμένους) by the nations, he does not bring us under (ὑπάγει) the consequence (ἀκολουθίᾳ) about worshipping such ones, whom the word/teaching (ὁ λόγος) shows (ἀποδείκνυσι) to be servants of the evil one (τοῦ πονηροῦ) and of the ruler (ἄρχοντος) of this age (αἰῶνος), who causes to stand away (ἀφιστάντος) from God whomever he can. As not servants then, all whom the rest of men revere, we decline (ἐκκλίνομεν) to revere and worship; for having been taught that they are servants of the God over all we would not say that they are demons (δαιμόνια). Therefore the one God and His one Son and Word and Image (εἰκόνα) we revere with supplications (ἱκεσίαις) and petitions (ἀξιώσεσι) as far as is possible for us, bringing (προσάγοντες) to the God of the universe our prayers (εὐχάς) through His Only-begotten; to whom first we offer (προσφέρομεν) them, asking Him, being 'propitiation (ἱλασμόν) of our sins', to bring as High Priest (ἀρχιερέα) our prayers and sacrifices (θυσίας) and intercessions (ἐντεύξεις) to the God over all. Concerning God then our faith (πίστις) [is] through His Son who confirms (βεβαιοῦντος) it in us, and Celsus cannot show any faction (στάσιν) of ours concerning the Son of God. And indeed we revere the Father, admiring (θαυμάζοντες) His Son, Word and Wisdom and Truth and Righteousness and all which we have learned the Son of God to be, so also the one begotten (γεννηθέντα) from such a Father. And these things thus.
pass_b_english: Then he thinks that, because we worship His Son together with God, it follows for us that on our own view not only God but also His servants are to be worshipped. Now if he had meant those who are truly servants of God after the Only-begotten of God, Gabriel and Michael and the rest of the angels, and had said that these ought to be worshipped, then perhaps, after clearing up what he means by worship and what acts the worshipper performs, we would have said on the subject, as men discussing matters so great, whatever we were able to understand about them. But as it is, since he takes as God’s servants the demons whom the nations worship, he does not bind us by any logic to worship such beings; for our teaching shows them to be servants of the evil one, and of the ruler of this age (John 12:31; 1 Corinthians 2:6), who draws away from God whomever he can.

So it is because they are not God’s servants that we refuse to revere and worship all those whom the rest of mankind reveres; for had we been taught that they were servants of the God who is over all, we would not call them demons. Therefore we revere the one God and His one Son, His Word and Image, with supplications and petitions as far as we are able, bringing our prayers to the God of the universe through His Only-begotten. To Him we first offer them, and we ask Him, who is “the propitiation for our sins” (1 John 2:2), to bring our prayers and sacrifices and intercessions as High Priest (Hebrews 2:17) to the God who is over all.

Our faith, then, is directed to God through His Son, who confirms it in us; and Celsus can show no faction of ours concerning the Son of God. And we do revere the Father, as we admire His Son, the Word and Wisdom and Truth and Righteousness, and all that we have learned the Son of God to be; and so we revere also Him who was begotten of such a Father. So much for this.

choices.choice: The staged text has ‘angels [archangels]’: the bracketed ἀρχαγγέλους (also bracketed in the Perseus TEI, line 18182) is marked by the editor for deletion and is not translated; restore ‘and archangels’ if review keeps it. ‘What he means by worship’ renders τὸ περὶ τοῦ θεραπεύειν αὐτοῦ σημαινόμενον (the sense of his ‘to worship’). ‘Our teaching’ renders ὁ λόγος (the word / the doctrine). ‘The ruler of this age’ combines John 12:31 (‘ruler of this world’) and 1 Corinthians 2:6, 8 (‘rulers of this age’); an allusion, not a quotation. ‘High Priest’ alludes to Hebrews 2:17 (compare Hebrews 4:14-15); ‘intercessions’ may echo 1 Timothy 2:1 (not cited). δαίμονας and δαιμόνια are both rendered ‘demons’. ‘Word and Wisdom and Truth and Righteousness’ repeats the titles of 8.9 (John 1:1; 1 Corinthians 1:30; John 14:6), not separately cited here as they are a list of titles.
none to the English: every clause matches the Greek (negations in οὐχ ὑπάγει, ὡς οὐχ ὑπηρέτας, οὐκ ἂν ... ἐλέγομεν, οὐδεμίαν ... στάσιν all kept; agency of ἀφιστάντος and βεβαιοῦντος correct)
checked 1 John 2:2 (ἱλασμός τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν), Hebrews 2:17 (high priest), John 12:31 and 1 Corinthians 2:6 (ruler(s) of this world/age) against the verses
